about: Community plugins for RackTicker: one folder each, installable straight from its URL. Add yours with a pull request — one entry pointing at a public GitHub folder that contains plugin.json.

plugins.name: Algorithms
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Computer science you can watch: two sorting algorithms race to put the same 64 shuffled bars in order, then a maze carves itself across the panel, a flood finds the way through and a runner takes the shortest path.

plugins.name: Arcade
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Ambient arcade: real games, played live by simple AIs at native resolution.

plugins.name: Asteroids
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Space rocks passing close to Earth this month, from NASA JPL: each one sweeping past the Earth and the Moon's orbit at its real distance, when it is closest, how fast and how big ('as big as a bus'). One passing inside the Moon's orbit takes over as it comes by.

plugins.name: Bar trivia
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Sports-bar trivia on the panel: a question, four answers, a countdown, then the reveal. Always fresh from the free Open Trivia DB and The Trivia API; a built-in set keeps it going offline.

plugins.name: Casino
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Games of chance that play themselves under the lights: Plinko chips rattling down through the pegs into the prize slots, and a slot machine spinning, stopping reel by reel, near misses and all, with a light show for a jackpot. No money, just the show.

plugins.name: Chess
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: A live game between strong players from Lichess TV, move by move: the board with the last move lit, both players with titles, ratings and running clocks, and the move just played in big letters. Free and open, no account.

plugins.name: Deep space
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: How far away our farthest spacecraft are, rolling like an odometer at their real speed: Voyager 1 and 2, New Horizons and Parker Solar Probe, with how long their radio signal takes to reach us, and Voyager 1's countdown to one light-day from Earth. From NASA JPL Horizons.

plugins.name: Departures
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Live station boards: the London Underground in its own line colours, Metrolink and Amtrak across the United States, BART, and seven European stations, each drawn the way that country's boards look, with trains pulling into the platform.

plugins.name: Derby night
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: A horse race that runs itself, sportsbook style: the tote board with the morning line, the gate, the field down the stretch with the running order, a photo finish when it is close, and what a $2 ticket paid. No betting, just the show.

plugins.name: Formula 1
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Formula 1: a start-light gantry counting down to lights out, the last race's podium and the championship fight. Key-free Jolpica (Ergast-compatible) API.

plugins.name: Space station
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: The International Space Station live: a lit world map with its track, what it is flying over and how fast, the crew's next sunset, who is aboard, and a take-over that tells you where to look when it crosses your sky.

plugins.name: Launches
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: The next rockets to fly, each with a countdown, its status and where it goes from. Launches you can see from home come first, with which way to look and a twilight flag for the glowing 'jellyfish'; ten minutes before one, the screen takes over for the count and liftoff.

plugins.name: Prediction markets
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Read-only public prediction-market odds board; no trading capability.

plugins.name: Now playing
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: The song you are listening to, like an old car stereo: album art, the title and artist scrolling past, track number and time, and a segmented spectrum analyser. From Spotify or any Home Assistant media player.

plugins.name: Onboard
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: The display above the carriage doors, for a train that is really running: the next stop in big letters, when it gets there, how fast it is going, whether it is on time, and the train moving along the line to it.

plugins.name: Quakes
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Earthquakes around you from the USGS: a 24-hour seismograph drum, the latest shakes by size and distance, and a take-over when a strong one hits nearby.

plugins.name: Retro Screensavers
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Classic desktop nostalgia in 128×32 pixels: growing 3D pipes, Mystify trails, starfield, a bouncing four-pane badge and marquee text.

plugins.name: Satellites overhead
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Every working satellite above your horizon right now, across the whole 360° sky and moving at its real pace: often a thousand at once, mostly Starlink. After dark the ones still lit by the Sun shine brighter; the space stations are named. Then the count by owner.

plugins.name: Sky
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Your whole horizon, 360 degrees across the panel: the Sun, the Moon, the five bright planets and the brightest stars where they really are, over a sky coloured by the time of day. Then the next twelve hours in eleven seconds, and when each planet rises and sets.

plugins.name: Space weather
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: What the Sun is doing to the Earth, from NOAA: the geomagnetic storm level with yesterday and the forecast as bars, the solar wind streaming past at its real speed, six hours of solar X-rays on the flare scale, and whether the northern lights could reach you.

plugins.name: Surf
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: The surf at your break: wave height, swell period and direction, water temperature, and real water — a simulated sea driven by the actual swell, sitting high or low with the actual tide.

plugins.name: Tanks
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Real levels as sloshing water: California's big reservoirs, and the space station's urine and water tanks when NASA's live feed answers.

plugins.name: Three bodies
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: The Sun, the Earth and the Moon side by side as they are right now: NOAA's newest picture of the Sun, the whole Earth from a weather satellite with today's clouds, and the Moon in its exact phase. Then the latest solar flare and the next full Moon.

plugins.name: LED sign
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Programmable LED sign: the storefront kind that spells words out of flying pixels, drops letters in, spins slot reels and chases marquee bulbs.

plugins.name: Freeway traffic
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Freeway traffic board: live CHP incidents on nearby freeways, shown as a freeway shield, what happened, where, and how long ago.

plugins.name: Data from a link
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Any number or text from a JSON web address, shown as a big clean card. No code: paste a link and the field to show.

plugins.name: Video player
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: Loops a short clip on the panel from a local file, a direct video URL, or any live stream ffmpeg can open. Give it several sources, or a YouTube channel, and it becomes a chill rotating channel.

plugins.name: Virtual Aquarium
plugins.author: Costa Mesa Tech Solutions
plugins.description: A living pixel aquarium: clownfish, angelfish, neon tetras, swaying plants and a wandering snail. Optionally mirrors real tank readings and lighting.
